tema: Quantifies health state utilities in people with ME/CFS in Australia and compares three instruments.
diseno: National cross-sectional survey of 198 participants with AQoL-8D, EQ-5D-5L and EQ-5D-5L-Psychosocial; DSQ-SF for disability and fatigue; Australian tariffs and Bland-Altman plots.
hallazgos: Mean utilities of 0.46 (EQ-5D-5L), 0.43 (AQoL-8D) and 0.44 (EQ-5D-5L-Psychosocial), far below population norms (0.89 and 0.77); they decreased with greater disability and fatigue; AQoL-8D and EQ-5D-5L-Psychosocial proved interchangeable.
conclusion: ME/CFS has a profound impact on HRQoL, roughly half the Australian norm; the EQ-5D-5L-Psychosocial is recommended because of its lower burden on the participant.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the conclusions add an explicit recommendation of the preferred instrument and highlight the importance of the psychosocial domains.

tema: Evaluates the psychometric properties of the PROMIS sleep and pain short forms in adults with ME/CFS.
diseno: Psychometric analysis of data from the Multi-Site ME/CFS Study (7 US clinics, 2012-2020): 945 participants at baseline (602 ME/CFS, 338 controls) and 441 with follow-up; reliability, DIF, known-groups validity and responsiveness to change.
hallazgos: Mean T-scores of 57.68 to 62.40 (about 1 SD above the norm); high internal consistency (ω = 0.92-0.97), no floor/ceiling effects or DIF by age or sex; worse scores than controls; pain interference showed acceptable responsiveness to change.
conclusion: The four PROMIS sleep and pain measures show satisfactory psychometric properties for use in research and clinical practice in ME/CFS.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the conclusions summarize the abstract and add their usefulness for evaluating treatment effects.

tema: Develops, through participatory research with the patient community, a comprehensive instrument to assess PEM in ME and CFS.
diseno: Community-based participatory research to design a survey, answered by 1534 members of the patient community.
hallazgos: Key PEM domains are identified, such as triggers, onset and duration of symptoms, which had not been comprehensively assessed by previous instruments.
conclusion: Collaboration between patients and researchers brings unique benefits for measuring the defining symptoms of ME and CFS and serves as a model of participatory research.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent on the value of patient participation. The conclusions (taken from the discussion, with noise from acknowledgements and funding) emphasize the collaborative and political dimension more than the findings on PEM domains.

tema: Analyses the association between symptoms and IgG concentrations against herpesviruses in ME/CFS and multiple sclerosis.
diseno: Reanalysis of data from the UK ME/CFS biobank: 222 patients in 4 subgroups according to trigger and 46 with multiple sclerosis; IgG against CMV, EBV, HHV6, HSV1, HSV2 and VZV; SuperLearner algorithm.
hallazgos: In ME/CFS, the most significant association was between IgG against HSV1 and brain fog; in multiple sclerosis there were more antibody-symptom associations; serology distinguished three ME/CFS subgroups from MS, but not the unconfirmed-infection one.
conclusion: IgG antibodies explain the symptomatology of multiple sclerosis more than that of ME/CFS; their clinical implication requires longitudinal studies.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract are consistent; the extracted conclusions are contributions, acknowledgements and abbreviations, with no conclusive content, so the conclusion comes from the abstract.

tema: Studies the T and NK lymphocyte phenotype as support for the diagnosis of ME/CFS.
diseno: Case-control study: 76 patients meeting the revised 2010 Canadian Criteria and 73 matched controls; immunophenotyping by flow cytometry and classification model.
hallazgos: Patients had fewer regulatory T cells and more NKT-like cells, lower NKG2C and higher NKCD69 and CD56bright NK; a model with NKG2C and Treg correctly classified 70% of individuals.
conclusion: The differences in T and NK subpopulations could define an immunological profile useful for diagnosis, although more studies are needed.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract are consistent on the diagnostic value of the immunophenotype; the extracted conclusions contain only contributions, acknowledgements and funding.

tema: Seeks to differentiate ME/CFS and long COVID by combining self-reported severity measures with circulating biomarkers of endothelial function and systemic inflammation.
diseno: Prospective, cross-sectional, single-centre cohort pilot study: 31 patients with ME/CFS, 23 with long COVID and 31 matched sedentary controls; 10-min NASA standing test; regression, principal component analysis and discriminant analysis.
hallazgos: ME/CFS patients had higher levels of serpin E1 (PAI-1) and E-selectin than both groups, and long COVID patients had lower TSP-1. TNF-α was elevated in both patient groups; in ME/CFS also IL-1β, IL-4, IL-6, IL-10, IP-10 and leptin compared with controls.
conclusion: The combination of biomarkers of endothelial dysfunction and inflammation with outcome measures differentiates ME/CFS and long COVID; more research on these mechanisms as possible targets is needed.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions are consistent; the PDF conclusions repeat those of the abstract (followed by introduction text). The initial result of the abstract appears truncated in the source.

tema: Systematic review of the associations between psychological and immunological variables in CFS/ME from a psychoneuroimmunology perspective.
diseno: Systematic review in PubMed (December 2020): 897 records, 14 studies included (807 participants), only two longitudinal.
hallazgos: Executive function was associated with IL-1 and IL-6, interpersonal function with IL-6 and TNF-α, emotional regulation with IL-2 and sleep with IL-1, IL-6, TNF-α and IL-2; poorer functioning was associated with more cytokines; only sleep-IL-6 and depression-IL-6 were replicated twice.
conclusion: Psychological-immunological correlations exist, but with few consistent findings and almost no longitudinal studies, which precludes firm conclusions.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the conclusions add that only two associations were replicated and propose sleep as a possible target, reinforcing the abstract's caution.

tema: To study whether the non-oxidative pentose phosphate pathway drives the elevation of BH4 in ME/CFS with orthostatic intolerance.
diseno: Pilot study: gene screening by microarrays, real-time PCR, ELISA and enzyme kinetics in ME + OI patients; human microglia model C20 with R5P and hypoxia and taldo1 silencing.
hallazgos: Enzymes of the anaerobic PPP and the metabolites BH4 and BH2 increased; taldo1 silencing inhibited GTPCH1 and BH4 production; plasma with high BH4 induced iNOS and NO in microglia.
conclusion: The non-oxidative PPP would be critical in the dysregulation of biopterins and could stimulate an inflammatory response in ME + OI.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract consistent; the conclusions text is administrative noise (ethics, funding), not available for comparison. Sample size is not stated.

tema: Validates the presence of autoantibodies against adrenergic and muscarinic receptors in plasma and cerebrospinal fluid of patients with ME.
diseno: Case-control study in two Swedish cohorts (24 with plasma and CSF; 24 plasma only) versus 24 controls (plasma) and 6 (CSF); IgG against α1-2, β1-3 and M1-5 by ELISA; severity by questionnaires.
hallazgos: Autoantibodies against M3 and M4 were elevated in both cohorts and against β1, β2, M3 and M4 in one; they did not correlate with severity and were not detected in CSF.
conclusion: A pattern of increased adrenergic and muscarinic autoantibodies is confirmed, with no evidence of intrathecal production, although their pathogenic role remains uncertain.
triangulacion: The three sources are fully consistent; the conclusions explicitly add the confirmation of previous findings in a German cohort and the absence of intrathecal production.

tema: Studies autoimmune gene expression and viral load in capillary blood of ME/CFS patients to look for severity biomarkers.
diseno: Cross-sectional study with recruitment through an app and social media: 166 patients and 83 healthy controls from the US with self-collection at home; expression panel of 51 autoimmune genes and PCR for HHV6, HHV7, CMV and EBV.
hallazgos: 49% of patients were housebound or bedbound. Bedbound patients showed higher expression of IKZF2, IKZF3, HSPA8, BACH2, ABCE1 and CD3D than mild and moderate ones, and more so if they had another autoimmune disease. Only 9 of 240 samples were positive for virus (8 HHV6 and 1 EBV).
conclusion: Gene expression biomarkers could differentiate subgroups according to severity and be therapeutic targets. Recruitment through social media with home sample collection would be an efficient research method.
triangulacion: The three sources agree on IKZF2, IKZF3, BACH2 and stratification by severity. The keywords highlight HHV6, although the viral results were marginal. The conclusions repeat the abstract and add a list of abbreviations.

tema: Evaluates whether hepatitis B vaccination in adults is causally associated with autoimmune diseases and with ASIA syndrome.
diseno: Literature review (1990-March 2017) and meta-analysis of controlled studies: of 1297 studies, 19 articles with 21 outcomes reviewed.
hallazgos: Controlled studies show no increase in the incidence or severity of autoimmune diseases after hepatitis B vaccination in adults.
conclusion: The absence of association calls into question the existence of the autoimmune/inflammatory syndrome induced by adjuvants (ASIA) as a clinical entity.
triangulacion: The abstract is the opening text of the article (truncated) and agrees with the keywords and conclusions; the work does not focus on ME/CFS, which does not appear in the sources.

tema: Analyses whether autoimmunity risk variants in immune genes are associated with ME/CFS, especially with infectious onset.
diseno: Genetic association case-control study: 305 ME/CFS patients and 201 healthy controls genotyped for five SNPs (PTPN22, CTLA4, two in TNF and IRF5).
hallazgos: The risk alleles PTPN22 rs2476601 (OR 1.63) and CTLA4 rs3087243 (OR 1.53) were associated with ME/CFS only in patients with acute onset after an infection, not in the others.
conclusion: Autoimmunity could play a role in ME/CFS with infectious onset; both genes regulate B and T lymphocyte activation.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract agree (PTPN22, CTLA-4, autoimmunity, SNP). The conclusions text (discussion) is administrative noise (ethics, funding, supplementary material), with no usable conclusions.

tema: Studies nocturnal cardiac autonomic function in the different sleep stages in CFS patients (IOM 2015 criteria) compared with tired controls.
diseno: Case series: 8 CFS patients and 8 tired controls (16-49 years); HRV, blood pressure and heart rate during polysomnography in all sleep and wake stages.
hallazgos: Patients showed more LF (sympathetic activity) in all sleep stages and less in wakefulness; less HF in stage N3 but more HF overall; higher nocturnal systolic and mean pressure and lower heart rate. There were no significant differences in the distribution of sleep stages.
conclusion: CFS could be associated with attenuated parasympathetic tone in slow-wave sleep and increased nocturnal sympathetic tone; more studies with IOM 2015 criteria are needed.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent around HRV, nocturnal pressure and sympathetic activity; the 'abstract' is the opening text of the article (truncated) and the conclusions are cautious given the very small sample size.

tema: Defines autonomic subgroups in CFS patients and their relationship to disease severity.
diseno: Cross-sectional study with 131 CFS patients (Fukuda criteria); fatigue scales, Epworth sleepiness and self-reported COMPASS; resting autonomic parameters (Task Force Monitor) and arterial stiffness (Arteriograph); factor and cluster analysis.
hallazgos: Four factors were obtained (fatigue, subjective and objective autonomic dysfunction, arterial stiffness) and four profiles: sympathetic with dysautonomia (34%), sympathetic only (5%), parasympathetic (21%) and altered sympathovagal balance (40%). The sympathetic-dysautonomic phenotype was associated with greater severity and poorer quality of life; the balance one, with younger patients, less fatigue and lower arterial stiffness.
conclusion: Autonomic phenotypes are strongly associated with severity; autonomic measurement should be part of the diagnosis and could justify differentiated treatments.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the PDF conclusions add the recommendation to measure autonomic function in the diagnostic process, not explicit in the abstract.

tema: Examines autonomic nervous system function, activity patterns and sleep after a physical or cognitive challenge in people with CFS.
diseno: Not stated in detail: the 'abstract' is only the cover page of the accepted manuscript; the discussion indicates participants from a specialized tertiary clinic subjected to physical and cognitive challenge protocols, with HRV measurement.
hallazgos: No detailed results are given; the discussion mentions that both challenges provoked a comparable exacerbation of fatigue and alterations observed in HRV.
conclusion: The authors point out that larger samples and additional covariates (e.g., mood symptoms) are required before establishing the mechanisms of the HRV alterations and their clinical implications.
triangulacion: Very limited sources: the abstract contains no summary and the conclusions are mostly limitations (bias toward more functional patients, pooling of challenges) and declarations; the keywords (HRV, sleep, heart rate) are consistent with the title.

tema: To profile PBMC bioenergetics and proteomics and relate them to symptoms in ME/CFS.
diseno: Exploratory study with 6 patients and matched controls; extracellular flux analysis, mass spectrometry proteomics and questionnaires on fatigue and autonomic dysfunction.
hallazgos: Severe fatigue correlated with autonomic dysfunction; PBMC with lower mitochondrial coupling efficiency and proteomic alterations centred on pyruvate dehydrogenase and coenzyme A.
conclusion: PBMC have a lower capacity to meet their energy demand; PDH dysfunction merits further study, along with its possible relationship to autonomic autoimmunity.
triangulacion: Consistent; the conclusions stress the small sample size and raise the link with autoimmunity of the autonomic nervous system.

tema: Explores bioimpedance spectroscopy of PBMC subjected to osmotic stress as a possible diagnostic technique for ME/CFS.
diseno: Pilot experimental study with PBMC from 4 patients and 4 healthy controls; device with interdigitated electrodes to measure impedance between 1 Hz and 500 MHz after osmotic stress with 1 M NaCl.
hallazgos: The device detected the presence of cells and the evolution of the osmotic process. At 1.36 kHz impedance was higher in patients than in controls; at 154 kHz there were no significant differences.
conclusion: Bioimpedance would be an affordable option with diagnostic potential, but more experiments are needed to confirm the results and explore patient stratification.
triangulacion: The three sources agree on bioimpedance, osmotic stress and diagnosis. The conclusions reveal the minimal sample size (4 + 4), absent from the abstract, and the lack of differences at 154 kHz, so they are more cautious.

tema: Science news article describing how the biological bases of chronic fatigue syndrome are emerging, focusing on microbiota and metabolic pathways.
diseno: News report (Nature); no study design stated.
hallazgos: Recounts Ronald Davis's work with a nanofabricated device: immune cells from six patients exposed to salt recovered worse than those of healthy individuals; describes that research suggests alterations of cellular chemical pathways and that the disease is no longer considered psychosomatic.
conclusion: Not stated (no conclusions section).
triangulacion: Only the opening text and the keywords are available; these mention microbiota and dysbiosis, which the fragment announces in the subtitle but does not develop; no conclusions are available.

tema: Systematic review of biomarkers that allow ME/CFS patients to be differentiated from healthy controls.
diseno: Systematic review according to PRISMA and Cochrane in PubMed, Embase and Scopus (1994-2022), observational studies in adults meeting Fukuda, CCC, ICC or IOM criteria; quality with JBI; 101 publications included.
hallazgos: The biomarkers were immunological (29.7%), genetic/epigenetic (19.8%), endovascular (17.82%), metabolomic/mitochondrial/microbiome (14.85%), ion channels and physical dysfunction (8.91% each) and neurological (7.92%); 79.2% were blood-based and the use of lymphocytes stood out.
conclusion: There is no consensus on a biomarker, but there is abundant evidence of immunological disruption; the use of NK cells as a model is supported and uniform protocols are called for.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the conclusions reinforce the role of NK cells and the view of interconnected systems, whereas the abstract stresses the poor reproducibility.

tema: Determines the diagnostic accuracy of NK cytotoxicity and DPPIV/CD26 as CFS biomarkers.
diseno: Case-control study: 176 patients and 230 controls; NK cytotoxicity by 51Cr release with K562 cells, lymphocyte CD26 by cytometry and soluble CD26 by ELISA; analysis with ROC curves.
hallazgos: NK cytotoxicity was significantly lower in patients and a good predictor; the percentage of CD2+CD26+ lymphocytes was elevated, but the number of CD26 molecules per cell and serum CD26 decreased; NK counts did not differ and CD26 did not correlate with NK cytotoxicity.
conclusion: NK cytotoxicity and the three CD26 measures are potential non-redundant biomarkers, relevant to the possible role of infection in the onset or persistence of CFS.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions are consistent; the conclusions reinforce the infectious interpretation and the evidence of T and NK cell activation. They include noise from figure legends.

tema: Analyses the relationship between clinical severity of ME/CFS, HHV-6A/B infection and autoantibodies against adrenergic and muscarinic receptors.
diseno: Case-control study: 134 patients (31 severe, 73 moderate, 30 mild) and 33 controls; HHV-6A/B PCR in blood and ELISA of anti-β2AdR, M3 and M4 AChR antibodies.
hallazgos: The HHV-6A/B genome was detected in 19/31 severe, 18/73 moderate and 7/30 mild patients; anti-β2AdR (1.4 vs 0.81 ng/ml; p = 0.0103) and anti-M4 (8.15 vs 6.45 ng/ml; p = 0.0250) were elevated with no relationship to severity; viral load correlated with anti-M4 and this with anti-β2AdR.
conclusion: A higher HHV-6 load is associated with a more severe course, and anti-β2AdR and anti-M4 antibodies support their use as biomarkers in the diagnostic algorithm.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the conclusions reproduce the end of the abstract. Stating that severity depends on viral load is a stronger causal interpretation than a cross-sectional design allows.

tema: Printed edition of a Diagnostics special issue compiling biomedical works that inform the diagnosis of ME/CFS.
diseno: Compilation book (edited by B. A. Lidbury and P. R. Fisher); no overall design stated.
hallazgos: The conclusions fragment, from one of the chapters, indicates that post-exertional malaise is associated with changes in glycolysis and acetylation, compatible with a hypoacetylation state.
conclusion: That chapter concludes that these changes could alter histone acetylation and cellular enzymatic control, and that well-designed studies are needed.
triangulacion: There are no keywords and the opening text is only the book's title; the conclusions correspond to a single chapter, so they do not represent the work as a whole nor allow triangulation.

tema: Compares blood volume in adults with ME/CFS according to whether or not they have orthostatic symptoms.
diseno: Preliminary study in 12 consecutive adults with ME/CFS; blood volume measurement with dual isotope and clinical assessment of suspected OI.
hallazgos: Mean blood volume was 59 ml/kg, 11 ml/kg below the reference. The 8 patients with suspected OI had significantly lower volumes than the 4 without OI (56 vs 66 ml/kg; p<0.05).
conclusion: Patients with ME/CFS and OI symptoms have lower blood volume; considering orthostatic symptoms could help detect the hypovolaemic subgroup, although larger studies are needed.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions are consistent around hypovolaemia and OI; the conclusions explicitly acknowledge the small sample size and add therapeutic implications.

tema: To detect brain microstructural abnormalities in ME/CFS using diffusion kurtosis imaging (DKI) and NODDI.
diseno: Prospective 3 T MRI study in 20 ME/CFS patients and 23 healthy controls; calculation of MK, NDI, ODI, FA and MD; comparison with two-sample t test in SPM12.
hallazgos: Decrease in FA in the genu of the corpus callosum and the anterior limb of the right internal capsule, with no differences in MD; decreases in MK and NDI in frontal and cingulate areas and the superior longitudinal fasciculus (SLF), and bidirectional ODI changes.
conclusion: Abnormalities of the right SLF could be a diagnostic marker of ME/CFS.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent (SLF, corpus callosum, FA); the conclusions come from the structured abstract itself, so they provide no independent information.

tema: Examines whether CFS patients with or without temporomandibular disorder (TMD) differ in brain responses to an autonomic challenge.
diseno: Exploratory 3 T fMRI study with Valsalva manoeuvre in 26 CFS patients with TMD, 16 with CFS without TMD and 10 age-matched controls.
hallazgos: In all groups the manoeuvre activated frontal gyri, putamen, thalamus and insula. CFS patients with TMD showed greater activity in the left insula compared with those without TMD and in the left caudate nucleus compared with controls.
conclusion: The greater cortical and subcortical activity during autonomic challenges could be modulated by fatigue and pain; autonomic dysfunction could contribute to both conditions, although more work is required.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions are consistent (Valsalva, insula, caudate); the conclusions are more cautious, acknowledge limitations of the exploratory design and focus on future paradigms.
